clue.text: Muse if there's time to

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone muses on what they would do if they only had the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder, but it is a noun: one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek goddess of lyric and love poetry, one of the nine Muses.

clue.text: A newspaper leader gets squeezed out

parts.note: the Express is a British daily newspaper
ED is short for editor, who leads a paper and writes its leader

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial is forced out.
explanation.definitionFit: To express juice is to press or squeeze it out.

clue.text: Weary of everything stylish?

parts.note: all means everything
in means fashionable or stylish

explanation.surface: Someone tired of everything fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal British for exhausted or tired out.

clue.text: The players' car others smash

definitions.note: the definition is possessive in the surface but works as the plain plural noun

indicators.note: a smash breaks things up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Musicians' car crashes into other vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is the company of musicians who play together.

clue.text: 9 reads list of numbers

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read over
a table is a list of figures, as in a times table

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a list of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 9 across is POLICEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest-ranking police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Senior officer and politician are set against one another

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: An officer and an MP are pitted against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare things is to weigh them side by side, examining their likenesses.

clue.text: Puzzle no more!

parts.note: non is a word for no or not
plus means more, as in extra

explanation.surface: A declaration that there will be no more puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus is to baffle or perplex someone.

clue.text: Diplomacy circumscribes one, that's understood

indicators.note: circumscribes means draws a line around, so the word for diplomacy surrounds the numeral

parts.note: tact is diplomacy in dealing with people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Diplomacy restricts someone, and that is taken as read.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied without being said, as in tacit agreement.

clue.text: For the confinement of the healthy young wife?

definitions.text: For the confinement of the healthy young wife?

parts.words: For the confinement of the healthy young wife?
parts.note: confinement suggests childbirth for a newly married woman in good health, but it means imprisonment, and the place's name splits into a fit newlywed

explanation.surface: Arrangements for a healthy newlywed giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridewell is an old British word for a prison or house of correction, after one in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell was a London jail whose name came to mean any lock-up or house of correction.

clue.text: Take in around a hundred and fifty to see brilliant display

indicators.note: around means the word for take in goes round the numeral

parts.note: to eat is to take in food
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Absorbing about 150 to witness a spectacular show.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is dazzling success or a striking show of brilliance.

clue.text: Complain nastily about a point made by 4 ac

indicators.note: doing something nastily twists it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles spitefully about an argument raised by somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange COMPLAIN with E (east, one compass point). The definition is a cross-reference: 4 across is CONSTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the most junior rank.

clue.text: Cold little church — unfortunate end

indicators.note: end tells us the word for unfortunate comes at the end of the answer

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
ill can mean unlucky or unfortunate, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: A small, cold chapel meets a sad fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a coldness in the air, so the noun or adjective can mean cold.

clue.text: Dicky, 22's man

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: 22 down is the woman's name IRENE

explanation.surface: A rickety fellow belongs to the woman in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram signal: British slang for unsound or wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a boy's name, short for Ernest.

clue.text: Grant for a growing concern

explanation.surface: A sum handed over to help a business that is expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing concern' sounds like a thriving business, but here it means literally growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a share granted or allocated, and also a small plot of land rented in Britain for growing vegetables.

clue.text: Surprise opening by the French

parts.note: a start is a beginning or opening
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A surprise opening by the French side, perhaps in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: The person who'll help Satanists to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form anew, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who will help devil-worshippers mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a helper or aide.

clue.text: Given direction, tot set out, though most unhappy

parts.note: S (south) is a compass direction
to tot up is to add

indicators.note: set out here means the letters of set are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A small child, told which way to go, sets off feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a child but is the verb to tot up. 'out' rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddest is the superlative of sad, meaning most sorrowful.

clue.text: Guides appear fearful about some rocky heights

parts.note: dire means dreadful or fearful
C (circa) means about
tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: Mountain guides look scared near some rocky crags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link but gives C, short for Latin circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors are those who steer, lead or point the way.

clue.text: Delay a seaman — have a meal on board

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to dine is to eat a meal
SS (steamship) stands for a vessel, and on board means aboard ship

explanation.surface: A sailor is held up while dining aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness or slowness, a delay in arriving.

clue.text: Break up underworld gang

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a band is a group or gang

explanation.surface: The police set out to break up a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests organised crime, but it is the mythological land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband is to dissolve a group so it no longer exists as one.

clue.text: Most profound nuisance at the bottom of the river

indicators.note: in a down entry, at the bottom of puts the nuisance under the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: The most profound nuisance lies on the riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest is the superlative of deep, used for the most profound thoughts.

clue.text: "Bound over" means something quite different to him!

definitions.text: "Bound over" means something quite different to him!

parts.words: "Bound over" means something quite different to him!
parts.note: in law bound over means ordered to keep the peace, but to an athlete in a race it means leaping over a barrier

explanation.surface: A court phrase means something else to a certain sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Being bound over is a British legal term for a court order to behave; here bound is taken literally as jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler is an athlete who leaps over barriers in a race.

clue.text: The married man's budget

explanation.surface: A married man's household spending plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a married man; to husband resources is to manage them thriftily, as on a budget.

clue.text: Worry about certain points there's" a need for airing

indicators.note: about means the word for worry goes around the word for points

parts.note: to fuss is to worry
tines are the points or prongs of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Fretting over details when a room really needs fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fustiness is mustiness or staleness, the stuffy quality of a room that wants ventilating.

clue.text: Bring pressure to bear in favour of the engineer

parts.note: for means in favour of
CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: Lobbying in support of the engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: To force is to compel by pressure.

clue.text: Their enemies include woman

indicators.note: include tells us the answer is contained within the words their enemies

explanation.surface: A woman counts among their foes.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Bill is in the Channel Isles to obtain plants

indicators.note: is in tells us the word for bill sits inside the islands' abbreviation

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the French coast
a bill passed by parliament becomes an act, so bill can mean act

explanation.surface: A man named Bill goes to Jersey or Guernsey to buy plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a parliamentary measure.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spiny desert succulents, the plural of a familiar kind of plant.

clue.text: Iron after tea and feel irritated by it

indicators.note: after means the symbol for iron follows the word for tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Ironing after teatime and getting annoyed with the chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to be vexed or impatient, as when rubbed the wrong way.

clue.text: Writer of review note

parts.note: to read is to look over or review
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone who writes a review note.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.

clue.text: Studied to be a real twister!

indicators.note: a twister turns things round, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that something is a genuine tornado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studied' is an adjective here, as in studied politeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Studied means carefully worked out and detailed, which is what an elaborate plan is.

clue.text: Made an appeal for leaderless men to be cared for

indicators.note: leaderless means the word men loses its first letter

parts.note: treated means looked after or cared for, as by a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded for men without a leader to be looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly, so the past tense means pleaded.

clue.text: Holds back supporters

explanation.surface: Someone restrains the people who back them.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem is to check or hold back a flow; stems are stalks that support leaves and flowers.
